newsitem.title: CHINA: Dow Chemical in China ethylene initial pact.
newsitem.headline: Dow Chemical in China ethylene initial pact.

text.p: Dow Chemical Co signed a letter of intent on Monday with China Petrochemical Corp (Sinopec) for a multi-billion dollar petrochemical complex to be set up in the northern city of Tianjin.
"We are quite confident that we will be able to work together to make this happen," a Dow Chemical spokeswoman said.
The two sides will have an equal share in the integrated ethylene and downstream derivatives project, to include a number of derivatives such as polyethylene, polystyrene, polyurethane and epoxy.
The project will be set up at Tianjin Petrochemcial Corp, a subsidiary of Sinopec.
Dow Chemical expected to complete its feasibility project by next year and saw start-up early next century, the spokeswoman said.
She described the venture as a multi-billion dollar project but declined to give a specific figure.
However, it would be significantly larger than Dow Chemical's existing joint venture chemical plant in the eastern coastal city of Ningbo, in which total investment was $70 million, she said.
Sinopec president Sheng Huaren said total investment for the project could reach between $3.0 billion and $4.0 billion.
However, a Dow Chemical official said the investment was expected to be closer to $1.0 billion. Officials were unable to clarify the discrepancy.
Annual output from the first phase of the project was forecast to be around 600,000 tonnes of ethylene, Sinopec and Dow Chemical officials said.
Dow Chemical officials said they hoped construction on the first phase of the project would begin in the year 2000, but gave no specific date for completion.
The bulk of production from the plant would be sold on China's domestic market, said Dow Chemical president and chief executive officer William Stavropoulos.
"It's the cornerstone of our future growth in China," Stavropoulos told reporters after the letter of intent was signed. "It's by far our biggest investment in this part of the world."
U.S.-based Dow Chemical is one of the world's major chemical companies and a leading producer of ethylene, Dow said in a statement.
Sinopec is China's largest petrochemical supplier and accounts for 85 percent of the country's crude oil processing capacity and 82 percent of ethylene production capacity.
